Internally Standardized Residuals for brma Objects

Source: R/residuals.R
rstandard.brma.Rd

Computes internally standardized residuals from a fitted brma object using the hat matrix or the corresponding known-V GLS/BLUP projection. Returns a data frame with raw residuals, standard errors, and standardized residuals (z-values). Available for normal outcome models only.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brma'
rstandard(
  model,
  unit = "estimate",
  conditioning_depth = "marginal",
  max_samples = Inf,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

a fitted brma object.

unit

output unit. Only "estimate" is implemented currently.

conditioning_depth

conditioning depth. Options are:

  • "marginal" (default): GLS projection residuals \((I - H)y\).

  • "cluster": Projection residuals after the fitted cluster contribution is removed. Only available for specialized multilevel models.

  • "estimate": Sampling residual projection after the fitted random-effect contribution is removed (a BLUP-style target).

max_samples

maximum posterior draws used for known-V brma.mv() marginal covariance computations. Defaults to Inf. Finite values deterministically thin draws across posterior row order.

...

additional arguments (currently ignored)

Value

A data frame with columns:

  • resid: Posterior mean projection residuals at the requested depth

  • se: Standard errors of the residuals

  • z: Standardized residuals

Details

This function returns a data frame with three columns matching the output of metafor::rstandard:

  • resid: Projection residuals: marginal depth uses \((I - H)y\); cluster and estimate depths retain their corresponding random-effect target. Known-V estimate depth uses the sampling residual projection. Residuals and SDs come from the same projection. These are not the posterior-mean residuals returned by residuals(type = "outcome"), which subtract the posterior mean of the fitted values and therefore carry the prior's shrinkage; the two agree as the effect prior becomes diffuse.

  • se: Standard errors of the residuals

  • z: Posterior mean of draw-wise standardized residuals

Internally standardized residuals are computed draw by draw by dividing the observed residual by its corresponding residual standard error from the hat matrix. The returned z column is the posterior mean of those draw-wise ratios, so it is not generally equal to the displayed resid / se summaries. For correlated known-V models, marginal residuals use the GLS residual covariance and estimate-depth residuals use the BLUP-style sampling residual projection. For a correctly specified model, these residuals should approximately follow a standard normal distribution. A design-exactly fitted row is set to zero only when its covariance multiplier has no other partners; fully saturated designs remain exactly zero under correlated covariance as well. Such a row has residual and standard error zero and an undefined standardized residual, so its z is NA (also when it is exactly fitted in only some posterior draws); qqnorm() omits these rows with a message.

For ensembles whose members differ in their PET and PEESE terms, each draw uses the design of its member, as described in hatvalues.brma.

This function is only available for normal outcome models without selection (weightfunction) bias adjustment. Selection models can use rstudent.brma, which uses LOO-PIT. Internally standardized residuals are unavailable for binomial and Poisson GLMMs because no count-likelihood standardization has been implemented. Use rstudent() (the LOO-PIT residuals) for GLMMs.

For known-V models, the standardized residuals require applying the inverse of the marginal covariance. A covariance that is too ill-conditioned for that (a reciprocal condition number of about 2e-10 or less in any posterior draw used) is unavailable: the call stops with an error of class RoBMA_known_v_precision_unavailable, whose parent class is RoBMA_numerical_unavailable, instead of returning a rounded number. The condition carries the draw positions (rows) and their reciprocal_condition. These positions refer to the current request after deterministic thinning, including estimate-depth requests.

See also

rstudent.brma(), residuals.brma(), blup.brma(), predict.brma()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(dat.lehmann2018, package = "metadat")
  fit <- brma(yi = yi, vi = vi, data = dat.lehmann2018, measure = "SMD")

  # marginal internally standardized residuals (default)
  rstandard(fit)

  # estimate-level (BLUP-based) residuals
  rstandard(fit, conditioning_depth = "estimate")
}
} # }
